Hi Patrick —

Great questions and thanks for the clear list. Recap and next steps below (summary for your procurement and infra teams):

1) Supported private connectivity
- We support provider-managed private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink, GCP Private Service Connect, Azure Private Link) for hosted Dedicated/private deployments.
- For Private (customer-managed) deployments we provide a control-plane connector and can support peering or customer-hosted endpoints depending on the deployment model.

2) IP allowlist / egress
- For hosted PrivateLink endpoints you do not need to allowlist broad egress ranges; connections are inside the cloud VPC. For hosted public endpoints we publish stable egress ranges (regional) — see attachment "redwood-vpc-endpoints-guide.pdf" for current ranges.
- If you must restrict egress from your VPC, common pattern is to route to a NAT/proxy with an outbound IP that you allowlist.

3) DNS & routing
- We recommend creating internal DNS records pointing to the PrivateLink endpoint DNS name. If you prefer an internal ALB, we can validate TLS and SNI requirements.

4) mTLS / certs
- Mutual TLS is supported for PrivateLink endpoints and required for some regulated customers. We can exchange certs via a secure transfer and support automated rotation on the Redwood side; customer cert rotation is on your side unless we host certs.

5) SDK / auth examples
- Typical server-side flow: service-to-service with an API key (Authorization: Bearer <token>) over the private endpoint. For tighter security we support short-lived tokens via our workload identity integration (OIDC) — Jonas will share examples.

6) Embeddings and reranker
- You can compute embeddings locally and store them on your side; calling our reranker/encoder over private endpoints works fine. If you want low-latency reranking we recommend colocating embedding lookup cache and using our batch/rerank API via the private network.

Next steps:
- I've looped in Jonas (solutions engineer) to provide specific IP ranges, DNS names, and mTLS flow.
- Please attach your network diagram (we can make specific recommendations).
- Propose a 1-hour technical deep-dive with our infra SME (Jonas + Dev) — are you available Fri 7/24 10:00-11:00 PT?

I've attached a short VPC endpoints guide and our Private quickstart for reference.

Best,

Patrick —

Adding a few implementation details from the SE side. High level recommendations below; we can walk through your diagram live on the call.

- Private endpoints: for AWS we'll provision an interface VPC endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce) which creates private DNS names in your VPC. You'll see elastic network interfaces in the endpoint subnet and security groups can restrict inbound calls. For GCP/Azure equivalents we use PSC/Private Link.
- IPs: interface endpoints use ENIs with private IPs — you don't need to open public IPs. If you're asking about outbound egress (calls from your VPC to external systems) and want a stable public egress IP, use a NAT Gateway or egress proxy.
- DNS: enable "private DNS" for the endpoint so the service hostnames resolve to private IPs automatically. If you override with an internal ALIAS/CNAME, ensure TLS SANs cover the name you present.
- mTLS: we support two modes: 1) TLS with client certs (mTLS) for the outer transport, and 2) token-based auth inside the TLS session. For mTLS we'll provide the CA chain and accept your client cert; rotation can be automated via our ops API.
- Firewall rules: allow outbound TCP 443 to our endpoint private IPs + any proxy NAT IPs you require.
- SDK auth sample: \n  curl -X POST https://api.private.redwood.acme.internal/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"claude-2","input":"Hello"}'

- Embeddings/rerank: if you store embeddings locally, you can call our /v1/embeddings or /v1/rerank endpoints over the private endpoint. Recommend batching for throughput.

I'll prep a short checklist for the call: subnet choices, security group rules, expected ports, DNS entries, and a cert exchange checklist.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber

Patrick —

Perfect, thanks for the diagram and checklist. Quick answers and confirmed next steps: \

- NAT/proxy egress: supported. We do not require any special configuration to accept calls from behind a NAT as long as the outbound IP is allowed in your firewall and you can present valid auth credentials. Jonas will include a short rule set for the proxy/NAT.
- Embedding provenance: we don't require a special header for embeddings, standard auth + request body is sufficient. If you want to signal provenance we can support an optional header (X-Acme-Upload-Id) that we persist to audit logs.
- PrivateLink POC: we'll provision a PrivateLink endpoint for your account. For the POC we'll use short-lived API keys and mTLS disabled initially; for production we can enable mTLS and workload identity.
